newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ROBSON HOPES TO CONCLUDE SUCCESSFUL WEEK WITH VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON HOPES TO CONCLUDE SUCCESSFUL WEEK WITH VICTORY.

text.p: Barcelona coach Bobby Robson, under heavy pressure from both press and fans, hopes to conclude a successful week with victory in Sunday's Spanish league match against Catalan neighbours Espanyol.
Robson's side knocked Real out of the Cup on Thursday but are still five points adrift of their arch-rivals in the Spanish championship.
Not surprisingly he hopes that the 4-3 aggregate win over Real could have important repercussions in the title race.

"Barcelona played a great game against a high quality team, we have demonstrated that we have ambition, capacity of sacrifice, and possibilites of winning the league," said the former England manager after the 1-1 draw. ''It was one of the most important games of my career.''
The game also featured the re-emergence of two players who have become scapegoats for the problems at the Camp Nou.

Goalkeeper Vitor Baia kept his side in the Cup with a series of key saves, while fellow Portuguese international Fernando Couto staked his claim to a regular place by marking dangerous Real forward Predrag Mijatovic out of the game.
Robson may give Couto the task of controlling Romanian Florin Raducioiu, who has rejoined Espanyol after a spell at London side West Ham.
Espanyol fans hope the return of Raducioiu will revitalise a side who have slipped to 16th in the league after finishing fourth last season.
But they are aware that Espanyol have not beaten Barcelona in league or Cup matches for nine years.
Earlier this season Espanyol led their more illustrious neighbours with just 10 minutes on the clock in the Camp Nou.
But Barcelona fought back to win, in an agonising repeat of the same fixture the previous season.
Espanyol took some revenge for that match in the return game by scoring a late equalizer which killed off Barcelona's faint championship hopes and helped seal the fate of then coach Johan Cruyff.
Robson took over from Cruyff, but is all too aware that even victory in the Cup may not be enough to keep him in his job, especially if Real take the league title.
Amidst rumours that Barcelona were lining up Ajax's Louis Van Gaal to take over from the Englishman, the club made public its support for Robson earlier this week.
For Barcalona fans the statement sounded all too similar to comments made by club officials last year, a few months before Cruyff was fired.
